content.title: How to watch the Rockets vs Lakers game without cable
content.text: Don't miss a second of the action when the Rockets take on the Lakers tonight.Billy CaddenThe Rockets return to Toyota Center on Wednesday night looking for a bounce-back win against the Lakers in a matchup with major playoff implications. Houston sits at 41-26 and holds the No. 4 seed in the West, but Monday’s 100-92 loss to Los Angeles tightened things up in a hurry. The Rockets are now 1.5 games behind the Lakers for the 3rd seed and just 2.5 games ahead of the 7th-seeded Suns, making every game down the stretch feel critical. With the standings this tight, especially among teams ranked three through seven, this is the kind of game that could swing postseason positioning.In Monday’s loss, Luka Dončić led the way for the Lakers with 36 points, and slowing him down will be priority number one for Houston. Kevin Durant was held to just 18 points, while Jabari Smith Jr. paced the Rockets with 22, showing that the supporting cast is capable of stepping up. Still, Houston will need more from Durant and a more complete defensive effort if they want to flip the result this time around. With LeBron James and Luka both capable of taking over a game, the Rockets will need to be sharp on both ends to protect home court and keep pace in the Western Conference race.The Rockets vs Lakers game tips off at 8:30 p.m. CST on Wednesday, and fans everywhere can catch all the action on Sling TV.When is Rockets vs Lakers? What: Houston Rockets vs Los Angeles Lakers When: Wednesday, March 18, 2026, at 8:30 p.m. CST Where: Toyota Center, Houston, TX TV: ESPN How to stream the Rockets vs Lakers game without cableAs the second game of a nationally televised doubleheader, the Rockets vs Lakers game will air across the country on ESPN. Since all of the streaming packages carry ESPN in at least one of their base packages, you can go with whichever streaming platform you want, but our top pick is Sling TV. Not only does Sling Orange carry ESPN and cost just $45.99/month here in Houston, but you can upgrade to Sling Orange & Blue and get half off your first month (just $32.50).While the monthly subscription cost is already cheaper than that of any other top streaming platform, the best value from Sling comes from its temporary access passes. Starting at just $4.99 for a 24-hour pass, you can get complete access to the Sling Orange library of channels, including ESPN. This is, without a doubt, the best way to check out the streaming platform and catch both national TV games.
